In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the confined complex channel floodplain system of the Yellow River responds to floods in a complex manner, and the response is related to the sediment transport coefficient, the degree of channel constriction, the pattern of floodplain confinement, the planform of channel wandering, and the sediment concentration of flood flow.

the confined complex channel floodplain system of the lower LYR is a highly dynamic system in which the channel is subject to both erosion and deposition, and the main and secondary alluvial plains are both accumulative.
the sedimentation and erosion of overbank floods are closely related to the channel boundary conditions and channel-floodplain morphology of the LYR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sediment transport coefficient and the ratio of peak flood discharge to the bankfull discharge are two key factors in determining the tempo-spatial sediment distribution in the confined channel-floodplain complex system of the LY.

the confined complex channel- floodplain system of the lower reach of the LY R responds to overbank floods in a different manner from that of the upper reach of LY R, which is mainly due to the difference of the boundary conditions of the channel and floodplain.
the sedimentation of overbank flow is mainly related to the channel planform pattern, while the channel boundary conditions play an important role in controlling the sediment erosion in the channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sedimentation/erosions in the confined complex system of the LY River are largely controlled by the ratio of peak overbank discharge to bankfull channel discharge, sediment concentration and the ratio of water volume to sediment load.
sedimentation/erosional processes are closely related to the overbank flood events, and the channel-floodplain interactions are largely controlled by the channel boundary conditions.
the channel boundary conditions along a river can significantly affect the response of the channel to floods, and the response is closely related to both the magnitude and duration of floods.
